questions.q: $K_a$ for $\mathrm{HCN}$ is $5 \times 10^{-10}$ at $25^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$. For maintaining a constant $\mathrm{pH}=9$, the volume of $5 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{KCN}$ solution required to be added to $10 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $2 \mathrm{M} \mathrm{HCN}$ solution is
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{p} K_a+\log \frac{[\text { Salt }]}{[\text { Acid }]}$
Let the volume of $\mathrm{KCN}$ solution required be $V \mathrm{~mL}\therefore \quad[\mathrm{KCN}]=\frac{5 \times V}{V+10}$ and $[\mathrm{HCN}]=\frac{10 \times 2}{V+10}$ Now from eqn. (i), $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{pH}=-\log \left(5 \times 10^{-10}\right)+\log \left[\frac{5 \times V}{V+10} / \frac{10 \times 2}{V+10}\right] \\ & 9=-\log \left(5 \times 10^{-10}\right)+\log \frac{V}{4}\end{aligned}$ On solving, $V=1.99 \approx 2 \mathrm{~mL}$

The concentration of $\mathrmH^{+}$at equivalence point is  \left(\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{w}}=1 \times 10^{-14}\right.$, at \left.25^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}\right)$,
questions.solution: $\mathrm{N}_{1} \mathrm{~V}_{1}=\mathrm{N}_{2} \mathrm{~V}_{2}$ (At equivalence point) $0.4 \times 2.5=\frac{2}{15} \times \mathrm{V}_{2}\mathrm{BOH}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{HCl}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow \mathrm{B} \mathrm{Cl}^{-}(\mathrm{aq})+\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}(I)\therefore \mathrm{V}_{2}=\frac{0.4 \times 2.5}{\frac{2}{15}}=\frac{0.4 \times 2.5}{2} \times 15=7.5 \mathrm{ml}\therefore$ Concentration of salt $=\frac{0.4 \times 2.5}{2.5+7.5}$ or, Salt of weak base and strong acid = $0.1\therefore\left[\mathrmH^{+}\right]=\mathrm{Ch}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{w}} \mathrm{C}}{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}}}=\sqrt{\frac{10^{-14} \times 0.1}{10^{-12}}}=\sqrt{10^{-3}}=3.2 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{M}$ as $C h^{2}=\frac{K_{w}}{K_{b}} \quad \therefore h=\sqrt{\frac{K_{w}}{K_{b} C}}$

questions.q: The $\mathrm{pKa}$ of a weak acid $(\mathrm{HA})$ is $4.5$. The $\mathrm{pOH}$ of an aqueous buffered solution of $\mathrm{HA}$ in which $50 \%$ of the acid is ionized is
questions.solution:
For buffer solution
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}+\log \frac{[\text { Salt }]}{[\text { Acid }]} \\
& =4.5+\log \frac{[\text { Salt }]}{[\text { Acid }]}
\end{aligned}$
as $\mathrm{HA}$ is $50 \%$ ionized so $[\text{Salt}]$=$[\text{Acid}]\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{pH}=4.5 \\
& \mathrm{pH}+\mathrm{pOH}=14 \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{pOH}=14-4.5=9.5
\end{aligned}$
Hence (C) is correct.

Solid ${AgNO}_{3}$ is gradually added to it Assuming that the addition does not change in volume and ${K}_{sp} ( AgCl ) = 1 . 7 \times {10}^{- 10}M^{2}$ and ${K}_{sp}\left({Ag}_{2}{CrO}_{4}\right) = 1 . 9 \times {10}^{- 12}M^{3} .$

\left[{Ag}^{+}\right] =$4 . 3 $\times {10}^{- 5}

questions.q: The $pH$ of an aqueous solution containing $1M$ benzoic acid $\left({pK}_{a} = 4 . 20\right)$ and $1M$ sodium benzoate is $4 . 5 .$ The volume of benzoic acid solution in $300mL$ of this buffer solution is __________$mL$.
questions.solution:
$\begin{cases} & Benzoicacid & + & Sodiumbenzoate & \\ Molarity & 1M & & 1M & \\ Volume & {V}_{a}ml & & {V}_{s}ml & \\ millimoles & {V}_{a} \times 1 & & {V}_{s} \times 1 & \\ & & & & \end{cases}$

$pH = 4 . 5$

${pK}_{a} = 4 . 20$

$pH = {pK}_{a} + log\dfrac{[ \text{salt} ]}{[ \text{acid} ]}$

$4 . 5 = 4 . 2 + log\left(\dfrac{{V}_{s}}{{V}_{a}}\right)Where, {V}_{s} - Volumeofsalt{V}_{a} - Volumeofacid$

$\dfrac{{V}_{s}}{{V}_{a}} = 2$..........(i)

${V}_{s} + {V}_{a} = 300$........(ii)

${V}_{a} = 100ml$

questions.q: Solubility of calcium phosphate (molecular mass, $M$) in water is ${W}_{g}$ per $100mL$ at $25 ° C .$ Its solubility product at $25 ° C$ will be approximately.
questions.solution:
Given the solubility of ${Ca}_{3}\left({PO}_{4}\right)2$ is $Wg / 100mL$. The solubility in $mol / L$ is $S = \dfrac{W}{M} \times \dfrac{1000}{100}mol / L$.

The equilibrium reaction of calcium phosphate is

$\begin{cases} & {Ca}_{3}\left({PO}_{4}\right)2 & \overset{}{⇌} & 3{Ca}^{2 +} & + & 2{PO}_{4}^{3 -} \\ Atequilibrium & & & 3S & & 2S\end{cases}$

Now, ${K}_{sp} = \left[{Ca}^{2 +}\right]3\left[{PO}_{4}^{3 -}\right]2$

$⇒ {K}_{sp} = \left(3S\right)3\left(2S\right)2 = 108 \times S^{5}$

$⇒ {K}_{sp} = 108 \times \left(\dfrac{W}{M} \times 10\right)5 ⇒ {K}_{sp} = 108 \times {10}^{5} \times \left(\dfrac{W}{M}\right)5$

$= 1 . 08 \times {10}^{7}\left(\dfrac{W}{M}\right)5$

questions.q: A weak acid of dissociation constant $10^{-5}$ is being titrated with aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution. The $\mathrm{pH}$ at the point of one-third neutralisation of the acid will be
questions.solution:
Hints: $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}=10^{-5} \Rightarrow \mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}=-\log \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}=-\log 10^{-5}=5\begin{array}{llcc}$& \mathrm{HA}+\mathrm{NaOH} \longrightarrow \mathrm{NaA}+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \\
\text { Initial } & 1 \mathrm{~mole} 0 & 0 & 0 \\
\text { Final } & (1-1 / 3) \mathrm{mole} & 1 / 3 \mathrm{~mole} & 1 / 3 \mathrm{~mole} \\
& =2 / 3 \mathrm{~mole} & 1 / 3 \mathrm{~mole}
\end{array} (Assumed weak acid to be monoprotic, since only one dissociation constant value is provided)
Final solution acts as an acidic buffer. \Rightarrow \mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}+\log $\frac{[\text { salt }]}{[\text { Acid }]} \Rightarrow \mathrm{pH}=$5+\log $\frac{\frac{1}{3}}{\frac{2}{3}}=$5+\log $\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \mathrm{pH}=$5-\log 2

questions.q:
The titration curve of weak acid vs. strong base with phenolphthalein as indicator is shown below. The ${K}_{\text{phenolphthalein}} = 4 \times {10}^{- 10}$

Given: $log2 = 0 . 3$

The number of following statement/s which is/are correct about phenolphthalein is _______

A. It can be used as an indicator for the titration of weak acid with weak base.

B. It begins to change colour at $pH = 8 . 4$

C. It is a weak organic base

D. It is colourless in acidic medium
questions.solution:
Phenolphthalein is an organic acid and can be represented as $HPh$.

$\mathop{HPh}_{\text{(colourless)}} ⇌ {H}^{+} + \mathop{{Ph}^{-}}_{\text{(Pink)}}$

Using Henderson equation for phenolphthalein

$pH = {pK}_{In} + log\left[\dfrac{\left[{Ph}^{-}\right]}{[ HPh ]}\right]$

At equivalence point  $\left[{Ph}^{-}\right] = [ HPh ]$

$∴ {pH}_{2} = {pK}_{In} = - log [ 4 ] + 10 = - 0 . 6 + 10 = 9 . 4$

Hence at $( 9 . 4 \pm 1 ) PH$ , phenolphthalein starts changing colour. Phenolphthalein is colourless in acidic medium and pink in basic medium. Phenolphthalein indicator distinguish the pH change between $8$ to $10$. Therefore, it is used for strong acid and strong base titration or weak acid and strong base titration. Hence, A and C are incorrect statements.
questions.source: Highly selective Backlog Qs for JEE Main

questions.q: Incorrect statement for the use of indicator in acid-base titration is:
options: Methyl orange may be used for a weak acid vs weak bas titration.
Phenolphthalein may be used for a strong acid vs strong base titration.
Methyl orange is a suitable indicator for a strong acid vs weak base titration.
Phenolphthalein is a suitable indicator for a weak acid vs strong base titration.
questions.solution:
Methyl orange and phenolphthalein indicators work with the change in pH and are termed as acid–base indicators.

Methy lorange is sutable indicator for strong acid vs strong base and strong acid vs weak base titration.

Phenolphthalein is sutable indicator for strong acid vs strong base and weak acid vs strong base titration.

There is no suitable indicator that can be used in the titration of weak acid and weak base. So, the correct option is A.

questions.q: ${K}_{a}$ for the reaction, ${Fe}^{3 +} ( aq ) + {2H}_{2}\text{O} ( l ) ⇌ \text{Fe} ( OH{)}^{2 +} ( aq ) + {H}_{3}O^{+}is 6.5 \times {10}^{- 4}$.~What is the maximum $pH$ value, which could be used, so that at least $80 %$ of the total iron  \left(III\right)$ in a dilute solution exist as ${Fe}^{3 +}$?$
questions.solution:
This problem is based on the conceptual mixing of equilibrium constant and $pH$ of the solution and given that,

${Fe}^{3 +} \left($aq\right) + 2{H}_{2}O \left($l\right) ⇌ Fe{( OH )}^{2 $+}\left($aq\right) + ${H}_{3}O^{+}\left($aq\right)$

${K}_{a} = 6 . 5 $\times {10}^{- 4}~and $80 %$ of~${Fe}^{3 +}$ present in the final solution means only $20 %$ is dissociated.

So,~\left[{Fe}^{3 +}\right] =$0 . $8Molarand\lleft[Fe\left(OH\right)2 +\right] = 0 . 2Molar$

~ ~ ~ & Now,& ${K}_{a} = \left[Fe \left($OH\right)2 +\$right]\left[{H}_{3}$O^{+}\$right] \left[{Fe}^{3 +}\right]

\text{6.5} \times$1{0}^{- 4} = \dfrac{0.20}{0.80}\left[{H}_{3}O^{+}\right]$

\left[{H}_{3}$O^{+}\right] = $\text{6.5} \times$1{0}^{- 4} \times4$

\left[{H}_{3}$O^{+}\right] = $\text{26.0} \times$1{0}^{- 4} = $\text{2.6} \times$1{0}^{- 3}$

\text{pH} = - \text\log \left[{H}_{3}$O^{+}\right]$

$= - $\text\log \left(\text{2.6} \times {10}^{- 3}\right)$

$= 3 - \text\log2.6 = \text{2.59}$

$
